guide: Forms 5.3.0 or later: read structure, existing links and natively authorized submissions. Aggregate creation is a separate forms.create tool in explicitly supported pins; existing objects are never edited by that tool. Native permission is rechecked per form. Shared expired or closed forms without results access may be absent from discovery but readable by id. Public participation links are credentials and appear only for native editors, including archived forms; the UI hides archived editing. Direct service calls do not inherit Forms dispatcher throttling. Response limits and every shortened field/list are explicit; oversized question/option structure is refused, never silently omitted.

Forms submissions require the separate forms.results grant and native results access: all permitted results or only the authenticated actor’s identified submissions. Respondent accounts are omitted, not personal data typed in answers. Only authorized answers to active questions and authorized files are projected, without omitted counts. Uploads also require files.read, Files scope and native READ on every actor-relative alias; no contents or new shares. UID 0 own mode is unsupported. Invalid UTF-8 in projected data and excessive pages are refused whole; no hard native-fetch memory cap or snapshot is promised.

forms_create_form requires forms.create and native creation permission. It creates a private form and its initial questions/options only in Forms 5.3.0, 5.3.7, 5.4.0 or 5.4.1. Preview is inert and confirmation repeats admission. It never edits caller-supplied IDs, publishes, shares, submits or sends mail. Native title synchronization may affect Files in 5.4.1; detected collisions stop after the empty form was created, and concurrent native effects remain possible. No extra Files grant or lock, rollback, retry or deduplication is implied.

Point editing uses forms.edit and native EDIT, independently of forms.create/results/read. Existing active questions/options only; no add, reorder or delete. One native PATCH per call, inert preview and explicit confirmation with plan_state; shared impact requires confirm_shared. A native 15-minute editing lock can identify the actor to other editors. Changing recipient email validation can make future confirmations ineligible and clear the selection, even when confirmations are already disabled. No reselection, enabled-flag change, sending or queued-job cancellation. Read receipts; concurrent edits/failures can leave a partial or uncertain update. Links are credentials. User text is untrusted.
